e7_s4_rationale: The patient's Holter monitor recording showed a gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block, resulting in ventricular asystole during syncope, which is consistent with Sick Sinus Syndrome.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Intrinsic Atrioventricular Block
e7_s4_rejected.why: The patient's electrophysiologic studies showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system, making intrinsic atrioventricular block less likely.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Progressive Cardiac Conduction Defect
e7_s4_rejected.why: There is no evidence of progressive conduction system disease, and the patient's symptoms are more consistent with a sinus node disorder.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Lev-Lenegre Disease
e7_s4_rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a prolonged PR interval and widening of the QRS complex, which was not observed in this patient.

e7_s4_rejected.label: His-Purkinje Disease
e7_s4_rejected.why: The patient's electrophysiologic studies and Holter monitor recording do not suggest disease of the His-Purkinje system as the primary cause of the patient's symptoms.
